title: Formulas with cached values ods 003
notes: OpenFormula cells with NATIVE cached values (the xlsx counterpart needs a zip rewrite because openpyxl cannot emit <v>; here table:formula and the cached office:value/string-value are authored together, no patching): IF cell: A1=9 (float), B1 carries of:=IF([.A1]>5;"big";"small") with a STRING cache — office:value-type="string" office:string-value="big" (no office:value) and display text:p "big"; the OpenFormula argument separator is the semicolon. The text:p child is the display string of the cached result — exactly what a cached-value extractor reads without recalculating. Honest caveat: LibreOffice recalculates of: formulas on load and reproduces these exact results, so recalc-vs-cache agree. The normative counter reads table:table=1; text:field stays 0 (table:formula is not a text:field).
